INS-001.note: php artisan sanitube:install — seven idempotent stages in the Installer module slot reserved since ARCH-001. The service is the installer so INS-002 can reuse it. Never overwrites .env, never replaces APP_KEY, always backs up at 0600, never takes a password as an option. UI-004.note: Four read-only ingestion screens. The candidate detail keeps four kinds of evidence apart: measured, claimed, noticed, decided. No object key, no disk, no bucket, and neither the storage driver's nor the analyser's failure message. Counts for a page come from one grouped query, asserted by a query count. Six regressions injected, every one turned a test red.

UI-005.note: Five read-only studio screens. Three provider states kept distinct — not configured is not a problem. Commercial rights UNKNOWN counted on the front page because nothing ever infers it away. No provider job id and no audio reference reach the browser; has_audio replaces the reference. Five regressions injected, every one turned a test red.

SYS-001.note: Operations and jobs screens behind can.role:administer. A GET probes nothing — proved by forgetting the snapshot, loading the page, and asserting it is still absent. No job payload and no stack trace reaches the browser; only the exception's first line, truncated. Unknown is not zero: an installation on Redis has no jobs table and the counts read null.

BULK-001a.note: Batch progress derived from the items, never stored beside them. One grouped count per batch, asserted. No percentage and no ETA — both would be invented.

BULK-001b.note: CSV manifest import + sanitube:import. A manifest is evidence, never authority: after importing 900 files naming 900 ISRCs, tracks and external_identifiers are both still empty. A bad row is refused with its line number; a bad file is fatal. An ISRC already active on another track holds the candidate NEEDS_REVIEW. Eight regressions injected, every one turned a test red.

notes.portability: $table->json() is forbidden platform-wide. MariaDB's json is an alias for longtext/utf8mb4_bin while MySQL 8's is a native binary type, so one migration yields two types with two comparison semantics. Use ->longText() with an Eloquent array cast. Enforced by PortabilityTest::no_engine_specific_construct_is_used_in_any_migration.
notes.capabilities: FFmpeg is a capability, never a dependency. SANITUBE_MEDIA_ANALYSIS_REQUIRED defaults to false so a cPanel host without ffprobe still produces promotable candidates.
notes.catalogue_writes: Promotion is the only v1 write that creates a Track. It always creates it DRAFT, mints no ISRC, and is refusable for six reasons each carrying a machine-readable code. One-master-one-track is enforced in PromoteTrackCandidate rather than by a unique index, because tracks is ARCH-002's validated schema.
notes.ci_triggers: The workflow only built pull requests whose base was main, so a PR stacked on another claude/** branch showed zero checks — indistinguishable from a repo with no CI. The pull_request branch filter now includes 'claude/**'. Fixed on the CAT-001 branch; it reaches main when that branch merges.
notes.migration_rollback: MySQL and MariaDB drop the index they generate for a foreign key once a user-created index can serve it. A migration that adds a unique index on an FK column must therefore drop the foreign key before dropping that index in down(), then restore it. SQLite enforces none of this, so a local rollback check on SQLite proves nothing about the server engines. Enforced by PortabilityTest::an_index_added_over_a_foreign_key_column_is_undone_in_the_right_order.
notes.ai_disabled_provider: The disabled AI provider is named 'none', never 'null'. Laravel's Env::get() turns the literal string null in a .env file into PHP null, so SANITUBE_AI_PROVIDER=null yields an empty provider name and the env() default never applies. Empty/absent/null configuration normalises to 'none' at AiManager::normaliseProviderName(); an unknown non-empty name is an error.
notes.no_hosts_in_php: PortabilityTest rejects any absolute http(s) host in PHP, config included. Vendor endpoints come from the environment with no PHP default; .env.example ships the public URLs.
notes.generation: Generation never creates a Track: a selected result becomes a VERIFIED asset and a TrackCandidate with source GENERATED, which CAT-001 reviews. commercial_rights_status defaults UNKNOWN and is never inferred from a successful generation. Polling is bounded twice — the job re-dispatches only while pollable, and the service fails the generation at max_polls.
notes.release_mutation: ReleaseMutationPolicy is the single place that says which edits a status permits. DRAFT allows everything; READY allows nothing structural but can be reopened to DRAFT; SUBMITTED/DELIVERED/LIVE/TAKEN_DOWN allow nothing and cannot be reopened. I4 is called, never reimplemented or relaxed.
notes.track_numbering: release_tracks carries UNIQUE(release_id, disc_number, track_number). Renumbering must be two-phase — park every row above the occupied range, then write final numbers — because a row-by-row update collides the moment a track moves into a slot another has not yet left.
notes.distribution: Submission is the one irreversible act. Three guards against a duplicate delivery: UNIQUE(release_id, provider), a guarded status UPDATE, and a derived (not random) idempotency key sha256(release uuid|distributor). Outage != rejection: unreachable and unconfigured both produce validation errors, an outage during submit leaves the delivery FAILED and retryable. DIST-001 never mints an ISRC or UPC — a missing one is a validation error.
notes.identity: Session auth on Laravel's users table. Three roles (OWNER/ADMIN/MEMBER). role and is_active are NOT mass-assignable — set them with forceFill. Wrong password, unknown email and deactivated account answer identically to prevent account enumeration. Throttling is per email AND per IP. No self-registration: accounts come from sanitube:user:create.
notes.translation_gate: tests/Feature/Localization walks EVERY file in lang/en and checks all configured locales both directions. Any new UI string needs en/fr/es/it/pt/de or CI fails.
notes.design_system: Semantic tokens only (--color-surface, never --color-zinc-900). Status colour is decided in StatusBadge alone; labels always come from translations. Navigation is built server-side and unbuilt sections show as disabled — 'available' is presentation, never authorisation. MetricCard takes number|null and renders null as an em dash, never 0.
notes.frontend_toolchain: @vitejs/plugin-vue@5 peers Vite ^5||^6; the project is on Vite 7. Resolved with plugin-vue@6 (which supports Vite 7), NOT --force or --legacy-peer-deps: a peer conflict is compatibility information, and overriding it keeps the incompatibility. Same for vue-tsc@3. npm run types runs in CI.

conventions_to_honour: Disabled providers are named 'none', never 'null' (AI, generation, distribution managers all share the rule).
$table->json() is forbidden; use longText + array cast.
No absolute http(s) host anywhere in PHP, config included.
A migration adding a unique index on an FK column must drop the FK first in down().
Every new UI string needs en/fr/es/it/pt/de; no hardcoded UI text.

A read model never returns an object key, a disk, a bucket, a provider job id or a provider's download reference. Prefer a boolean that answers the question (has_audio, has_manifest_row) over the value itself.
A failure *code* is translated and shown; a failure *message* from a storage driver or an analyser is withheld, because it quotes a path. A provider's own message about its own service is kept.
Counts for a page come from one grouped query, never one per row, and every enum state is present including the zeroes.
Every list validates that a cursor describes its own ordering via CursorShape, including lists that take no filters.

A controller never writes a status. If the behaviour lives in a controller today, extract it to a service both surfaces call rather than copying it — and prove the extraction by running the existing tests unmodified.
Authorisation lives on the route (can.role:catalogue / :administer). An `actions` block in a payload is presentation, and a test must prove hiding a button is not what stops a request.
A refusal travels as its machine-readable code; the interface translates it. The domain's English sentence is written for a developer reading a log.
A preflight check asks what the machine can do; a health check asks what this installation has done. Do not block the first on the second.
When two layers guard the same rule, mutate the inner one — a passing service-level test can hide an unguarded method a later surface will call directly.
No financial calculation anywhere. A credit or ownership field is metadata; it never becomes a right to money.
The domain carries no distributor-specific logic. Provider specifics belong in adapters.
A LIKE search escapes % and _ with an explicit ESCAPE clause; the escape character is ! because MySQL also treats a backslash as an escape inside string literals and SQLite does not.
A screen never probes an external provider on render. Availability and sandbox mode come from configuration; asking the provider anything is a button.
UNKNOWN, FAILED and REJECTED are three different things and are never drawn the same way. An outage is not a verdict.
A provider job id, external reference or idempotency key never reaches a payload. Prefer a boolean that answers the question (has_external_reference).
A credential is reported as configured or not configured. Never a value, never a mask, never a length.
Read presence through config, not env(): a config:cache-d installation gets null from env() for everything.
A deploy creates nothing an install would create. Missing .env, key or database is a refusal with its reason, never a silent fix.
A guard that reads a file as text will trip on a comment naming what it forbids. Reword the comment, never weaken the guard.

An assertion must fail for the reason it names. Nine defective tests this session were satisfied by something other than the thing they checked — a comment explaining a flag, a neighbouring path, prose about a setting.
Documentation that has not been verified against a real host says so in its first paragraph, and a test keeps it saying so.

asset_preview_url.rule: No signed URL is ever included in the Asset detail payload at page load.
asset_preview_url.why: A signed URL is a temporary bearer credential. Minting one on every detail view needlessly widens its lifetime and its exposure surface.
asset_preview_url.flow: Asset detail -> user clicks Preview -> authorised UI action -> backend verifies permission and asset kind/status -> mints short-lived signed URL -> browser receives it
constraints: never disk, path, bucket or credentials
VERIFIED required for an audio master
minted on demand, never on the detail GET
URL never persisted in the database
full URL never written to logs
if the provider cannot issue temporary URLs: show Preview unavailable, never make the object public

known_limitations.where: All five catalogue index filter forms
known_limitations.what: A refused filter answers 422 with a JSON body rather than an error rendered inside the form.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: Refusing loudly is what must not regress; presenting it nicely needs inline error display.
known_limitations.priority_note: Now applies to five lists rather than two, which raises it.

known_limitations.what: Orderings are (natural key, uuid) with no composite index over the pair.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: Not measurable at target catalogue sizes; a migration belongs in a CAT ticket with a measurement behind it.

known_limitations.what: Re-importing the same reference writes a second asset row and a second stored object, which the checksum then resolves to the first. Nothing reaches the catalogue — no Track, no identifier, and the candidate is DUPLICATE — but re-running a 900-file manifest stores 900 objects twice.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: The current behaviour is defensible: ING-001 re-reads the source rather than assuming a reference imported yesterday still holds the same bytes today, and an object genuinely can be replaced under its key. Skipping on the ingestion key alone would silently miss that replacement — a data-loss trade in the opposite direction.
known_limitations.pinned_by: two tests in ManifestImportTest pin the current behaviour, so whichever way it is later decided the change is visible

known_limitations.what: sanitube:install is covered by 21 tests against a temporary .env and was smoke-run in the development container, but has never been run on a real cPanel account against a real MySQL database.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: No such account is available to this project. The stages that would differ are the ones that touch the host: directory permissions, the PHP binary path in the cron line, and the account-prefixed database names.
known_limitations.severity: blocks calling installation production-ready, nothing before then

known_limitations.where: ValidateRelease, Release::readinessProblems(), the release builder screen
known_limitations.what: Validation errors and warnings are English sentences, not codes, so they render untranslated on the five non-English locales while the rest of the screen is translated.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: The same strings are imploded into delivery-attempt records and matched on by SubmitDelivery::wasUnreachable(). Turning them into codes changes delivery semantics, which is a domain ticket (REL-002), not something a UI ticket does quietly.

known_limitations.what: The preflight’s errors and warnings are the same untranslated domain sentences the release builder shows.
known_limitations.why_not_fixed: ValidateDelivery merges ValidateRelease’s output with its own and SubmitDelivery::wasUnreachable() matches on the text. Same root cause, same ticket.

bulk_001_scope.finding: BULK-001 is much smaller than its ticket assumes. ING-001 already provides batches, per-item state, idempotent retry via UNIQUE(ingestion_key, active_marker), attempt_count, per-item failure codes, CompletedWithErrors as a first-class outcome, the processing and finalising jobs, StartIngestionBatch::handle() taking a prefix or explicit references, and CloudImportReader.
bulk_001_scope.instruction: DO NOT create a BulkImportBatch table or any parallel import path. Two mechanisms both claiming to prevent duplicate imports is worse than one — the second is the one nobody tests against a real retry.
remaining: DONE — an interface entry point to start a batch from a prefix or a manifest (BULK-001b, sanitube:import)
DONE — UI-004, which renders this progress read model

preflight_vs_history.severity: would have refused every first install
preflight_vs_history.finding: The scheduler capability reports unavailable until a cron entry has fired at least once. Preflight blocking on it meant a first install could never pass, because the condition cannot be true before the installation exists.
preflight_vs_history.instruction: A preflight check asks whether the machine CAN run SaniTube. A health check asks whether this installation IS running. The same detectors serve both, but a capability describing the installation's history is not a prerequisite. InstallationService::NOT_PREREQUISITES names the two exclusions with their reasons; keep the list short, because a preflight that skips checks stops meaning anything.

guard_covered_at_only_one_level.severity: a defective test that read as a passing one
guard_covered_at_only_one_level.finding: The mutation removing the overwrite guard from EnvironmentFile::createFromExample() stayed green, because InstallationService checks exists() before ever calling it. The service-level test covered the behaviour; nothing covered the guard.
guard_covered_at_only_one_level.instruction: When two layers both guard the same thing, the mutation must be run against the inner one. INS-002's web installer reaches EnvironmentFile without the service's outer check, so the inner guard is the one that will matter. A direct test now covers it.

scope_correction_v1.statement: SaniTube is a music catalogue and distribution platform. It is NOT a financial platform.
scope_correction_v1.still_in_scope: Rights and credit information strictly necessary for distribution, as catalogue metadata only: author, composer, publisher (as metadata), copyright, the P and C notices, declarative master ownership, contributor roles, ISRC, UPC/EAN, territories, explicit content, language, credits. None of it may trigger a financial calculation.
scope_correction_v1.existing_code: Not deleted. No Revenue/Royalty/Payout/Ledger module was ever built, so nothing has to be removed; the tickets are reclassified instead.
scope_correction_v1.multi_distributor: The domain must contain no logic specific to TuneCore, Too Lost, DistroKid, CD Baby or Ditto. Provider specifics live in adapters. No TuneCore API is assumed to exist, and scraping is never an API substitute.
scope_correction_v1.navigation: `publishing` and `royalties` removed from the sidebar in DIST-UI-001, with their translation keys and icons. Both were placeholders for financial administration. `rights` stays, unavailable: credit and ownership metadata is required for distribution and is not a right to money.
